written: 2026-10-31, after stage 1 (its eight readings at 0.16 mm and its probe) and before any solve of M1's ladder. No ladder value is known: the probes read no speed.
what_happened: Stage 1's probe of 0.1024 mm ran out of device memory: one 14.54 GiB allocation (one matrix) refused while the solve was autotuned, against JAX's default preallocation of 75% of the device (bytes_limit 63.8 GB on the A100-80GB, about 59.4 GiB). The probe of 0.128 mm fitted (peak 62.7 GB of 63.8). By the committed rule the ladder would be 0.25, 0.2, 0.16, 0.128 mm.
why_an_addendum: The failure is the allocator's share, not the device: the register's B5 item 1 asks the ladder to end at the finest affordable, and the committed fallback was written for a level that does not fit the device. Raising the share is not a change to any computation.
rule: One more probe of 0.1024 mm with XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.95, exercising every program a level runs (the assembly with the wall, two solves at blob 0.5, and the node's own step); it reads no speed. If it fits, the ladder is the committed first choice, 0.2, 0.16, 0.128, 0.1024 mm; if not, the committed fallback, 0.25, 0.2, 0.16, 0.128 mm. Every ladder level then runs with the same 0.95 share. The predictions of stage2_M1 stand unchanged for either ladder.
stage2_cost_rule: Stage 2's upper estimate is taken from the measured times: 0.90 s per node step at 0.16 mm and 1.20 s per solve at 0.128 mm (stage 1), the probe's solve time at the finest level, about 1.5 s per Volume save (stage 1's phase deltas, 2.4 s against a 0.9 s step), and a level's compilation; the sum times the container's $2.817 per hour, times 1.4.
run_control: A level whose nominal reading is indefinite or non-finite, or whose wall read is refused, stops itself and is recorded; the stage goes on to the next level (it had stopped the stage, which would have cut the ladder at its coarsest level). Only the deadline stops the stage. M1's analysis counts only complete levels, so a stopped level leaves fewer than four spacings and the band unbounded, as B5 says.
